A.title: Everyday travel
A.body: First, please tell us about the transport options you currently use and the types of journeys you make. These questions are about your actual circumstances; there are no right or wrong answers.

purposes.title: The different journeys you make
purposes.body: The same person may use different transport modes for commuting, errands and leisure. The next two questions ask about these purposes separately. There is no assumption that everyone works, studies or makes weekly leisure journeys.

journey.title: One ordinary journey
journey.body: For the next questions, think of ONE real journey you make regularly, using the purpose groups above. We will return to this same ordinary journey after the 2030 choice experiment. Do not use the hypothetical 20 km trip as your reference. Prefer a journey you make at least weekly; otherwise choose the most regular journey you have made in the past four weeks.

B.title: A future trip in 2030
B.body: The next questions concern a hypothetical 20 km one-way weekday trip in 2030. This trip is separate from the ordinary journey you just described.

scenario.title: Imagine the same 20 km trip
scenario.body:
Imagine one adult making the same 20 km one-way weekday trip in 2030. Each option shows the total amount your household would pay for that trip, total door-to-door time, the chance of arriving within five minutes of the planned time, and walking/wheeling time. Walking/wheeling and waiting are already included in total time. Costs are stated in current-purchasing-power euros.

Consider driving only if you could legally drive, or travelling as a passenger only if an authorised household driver is available. A private or shared EV here is a household arrangement, not a promised autonomous taxi. Consider public transport only where an accessible service is feasible. If no displayed offer suits you, choose “None of these.”

C.title: Return to your ordinary journey
C.body: Now return to the ordinary journey you described earlier. The next statements ask about one transport option you might use more often, or continue using, for that ordinary journey—not about the hypothetical 2030 trip.

D.title: Vehicles, parking and charging
D.body: The next questions are about your current circumstances. You do not need to own a vehicle or charge one yourself. Questions about actual plug-in vehicle charging will appear only when they are relevant to your household and you can describe the arrangements.

programming_notes: C-ALT-USED explicitly confirms the non-private-car mode after C-ALT-01=already using; no mode is assigned silently.
Journey-purpose selection is respondent-chosen in this prototype. Production balancing is not implemented.
No recurring ordinary journey skips journey-dependent COM-B; it does not remove transport-DCE eligibility.
Unknown alternative mode skips dependent ratings; current-mode habit can still be shown when the ordinary current mode is known.
A-PARK-CHG uses existing/future vehicle context as the provisional relevance rule; no home ownership requirement.
A-CHG-OUT and A-CHG-SCHED are included optional modules from the draft, so their timing can be reviewed.
PCAP is included only in this private draft walkthrough. Its production ethics/data-protection activation remains a later decision.
